text:
maya: heads up — p99 spiked on canary during the 8k qps stress test, reproducer attached
jordan: saw that in dashboard. p50 ~45ms, p95 ~180ms, p99 jumped to ~920ms for ~30s window :grimacing:
maya: root cause initial guess: cache rebalancer + microbatching interacting badly under high concurrency. stack traces show fallback to generic kernel
li: can you drop the profiler snippet? we need a quick flame
maya: pasted perf snippet from canary host:
```text
PID  TID  CPU%  FUNC
1234 1234  42.1  runtime::generic_matmul_kernel
1234 1235  28.3  kvcache::evict_worker
1234 1236  10.2  runtime::select_kernel
```
maya: note generic_matmul lines start when select_kernel returns code 7 (kernel mismatch) and we see concurrent evicts thrashing KV hotset
samir: reproduction command I used:
```bash
ab -n 20000 -c 200 http://canary.redwood/api/v1/generate -T 'application/json' -p small_prompt.json
```
jordan: microbatch config on canary was `microbatch_size=16, max_batch_wait=15ms`
li: with that MB and a hotset churn, KV cache eviction latency cascades; requests miss KV and then get forced to recompile/route kernel
maya: observed kernel fallback latency ~3.2x vs optimized path. CPU spikes match evict thrash
samir: quick mitigation rolled: lowered microbatch to 8 and added eviction hysteresis 500ms. deployed canary at +5
perf-bot: deploy canary-evict-hysteresis rolled to 10% hosts
maya: after mitigation p99 fell to ~210ms within two minutes, p95 ~170ms stable
jordan: long-term: two ideas
 - adapt microbatch size by hotset-pressure signal
 - avoid immediate kernel fallback if eviction in last 1s (grace window)
li: +1. Also recommend changing kernel selection to prefer pre-compiled safe kernel for small sequence lengths instead of falling back to slow generic
samir: I'm going to instrument `kvcache.hitrate` and expose an SLO signal to runtime router and add a microbatch throttle controller
maya: assigning follow-ups:
 - samir: add hysteresis + telemetry (PR up next) 
 - li: prototype kernel-selection fallback window
 - jordan: run wider canary (30% traffic) after PR
maya: thanks. saved logs and perf traces in /mnt/artifacts/2150001234/
jordan: FYI, we need an eng-sre postmortem if this hits prod SLA. for now put incident tag `latency-surge-2150001234`
samir: PR: https://git.redwood/repo/infra/+/3456 — adds eviction_hysteresis_ms and mb_autoscale hook
li: test notes: local bench shows steady-state throughput loss ~5% with microbatch=8 vs 16 but p99 wins 4x under KV churn
maya: will follow up with full analysis and flame graphs tomorrow :coffee:
perf-bot: automatic alert cleared after 12m
